input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: After stripping ANSI codes the prompt text is also passed through str.strip(), which removes the whitespace at the end of the prompt that separates it from the user's typed input.
- failure path: click.prompt("Name") builds the prompt 'Name: '; when the stream does not support color (piped output, CliRunner, NO_COLOR) the prompt is shown as 'Name:' with the cursor glued to the colon, while on a color-capable terminal the same call keeps the trailing space, so transcripts differ between the two environments.

Reviewer finding
- description: The new code calls .strip() on the prompt text, which removes trailing whitespace as well as the ANSI codes, so a prompt such as "Name: " is passed to input() as "Name:".
- rationale: Trigger: prompt("Name: ") or confirm("Continue? ") runs while the destination stream is not a TTY, so should_strip_ansi returns true even if the text has no ANSI codes. Mechanism: strip_ansi(text).strip() drops the trailing space, so the prompt is shown with no separator before the cursor. Impact: non-TTY and CliRunner output changes for every prompt that ends in a space, and tests that compare that output will fail. Only the ANSI removal was intended, so the whitespace trim is an unintended side effect.
critique: The finding points to the same cause: .strip() after strip_ansi in the non-color path removes the trailing space, so 'Name: ' turns into 'Name:' when output goes to a non-TTY or CliRunner. That is the same faulty operation, failing the same way.
